app/lib/format.js:9-33 — humanize/enName/latestEnFlavor/enEffect/dexNumber, all pure and trivially testable, untested
app/app/page.js:38-76 — filter pipeline, page clamping and pageHref URL assembly untested
coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist at all, so none of the riskiest logic — data transformation, URL state, caching, error paths — is covered by the app's own suite.

evidence: app/ — zero test files anywhere in the source tree (only .next/ build artifacts reference Playwright)
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: There are no tests, so the criterion cannot be met; the app contributes nothing behavioural or otherwise.

evidence: app/lib/api.js:17-37 — hand-rolled concurrency limiter (waiter queue, inFlight counter) is refactor-fragile and unguarded
app/lib/api.js:51-60 — cached() evicts rejected loads so retries succeed; caching a rejection forever would break the app permanently with no test failing
app/app/Controls.js:34-46 — debounce timer closes over stale typeValue/generationValue; the resulting filter-revert bug already exists and nothing would catch it
regression_power.rationale: With no tests of its own, any regression in the data layer, URL handling or client state passes silently; the app even ships a latent debounce race today.

evidence: app/ — no test files; nothing to pad with, nothing to maintain
signal_to_noise.rationale: Per the rubric, an app with no tests scores 3 on signal-to-noise: zero noise, but also zero signal.

findings.issue: The 300ms debounce captures typeValue/generationValue from the render at typing time; changing a select inside the window makes the later timer re-apply the stale values and silently revert the user's filter in the URL. No test would fail on this today.
findings.suggestion: Fix by merging pending updates into a ref of the latest filter state, and add a client test that types then immediately changes the type select and asserts the resulting URL keeps the selected type.

findings.issue: mapToSpecies encodes the app-wide contract (alternate-form exclusion, species-index membership, dedup, dex order) used by every card list; it is completely untested, so a refactor reintroducing Mega forms or dropping the sort would slip through.
findings.suggestion: Unit test with refs to id 10025 (excluded), an id not in the species index, duplicates, and out-of-order ids, asserting the exact output array.

findings.issue: limitedFetch's semaphore and cached()'s evict-on-rejection retry semantics are hand-rolled concurrency logic with no coverage; a subtle refactor (e.g. caching the rejection, or losing the waiter shift) produces deadlocks or permanently-cached failures that only manifest under load or during API hiccups.
findings.suggestion: Add tests for: a rejected fetch is not cached and a second call retries; 404 resolves to null and IS cached; more than MAX_CONCURRENT concurrent fetches all complete.

findings.issue: humanize, enName, latestEnFlavor, enEffect and dexNumber are pure functions embodying spec definitions (whitespace collapse, last-English-entry, #0000 padding) — the cheapest possible tests to write, and none exist.
findings.suggestion: Add a small unit test file covering hyphenated names, empty/missing names arrays, trailing whitespace and \n/\f in flavor text, and 1/25/10025 padding.

findings.issue: The filter/pagination pipeline — combined q/type/generation filtering, the page>totalPages clamp, and pageHref's default-omission rules — is untested URL-state logic; a refactor dropping the clamp or emitting page=1 explicitly would break deep links like /?type=fire&generation=generation-i.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the pure parts (pageHref construction, clamping) and one integration case for a multi-filter URL with a bogus page number.

findings.issue: compareValues implements missing-values-last in both directions plus numeric-vs-string comparison, and the aria-sort state machine; a flipped comparison or missing-value regressions would only be caught by the acceptance suite, if at all.
findings.suggestion: Extract compareValues and the toggle reducer into a testable module and unit-test missing-last in both directions, descending numeric sort, and toggling to descending.

findings.issue: buildMovesSection handles version-group ordering by `order`, the known-method-then-alphabetical method comparator, and default row sorting — dense ordering logic with no tests.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the method comparator (known methods in METHOD_ORDER order, unknown ones alphabetically after) and the row sort with null power/accuracy values sorting after populated ones.

findings.issue: Damage-relation term order and the 'None' empty case, plus the moves list's humanized-name sort, are untested; a reordered RELATIONS array or dropped 'None' would render wrong silently.
findings.suggestion: Add a data-driven test asserting the six terms in spec order and 'None' for empty relations, and that the moves list is sorted by label.

findings.issue: Not-found behaviour (loadPokemonPage returning null → notFound) and the height/weight /10 + toFixed(1) formatting are untested error/format paths; a refactor swallowing the null or dividing by 100 yields wrong pages with nothing failing locally.
findings.suggestion: Add tests for an unknown species name producing the Not found h1 and a link to /, and for height/weight formatting of decimetres/hectograms.

summary: The app ships zero tests of its own; every guarantee rests on the harness-provided acceptance suite, which the team won't own. The untested code is precisely the riskiest kind — a hand-rolled fetch cache/limiter, multi-step data mapping, URL-state filters and client-side sorting — and at least one latent bug (the debounce race in Controls.js reverting a just-chosen filter) is already present and undetectable by anything in app/. A focused unit-test file for lib/api.js, lib/format.js and the sort/filter logic would be a few hundred lines and would guard most of it.
